bull.b: Independent DSMB clearance to escalate dosing and full enrollment at the 10 mg cohort materially reduces near-term development risk for the lead program. Multiple planned readouts (Nov 2026 and H1 2027) create discrete clinical milestones that can de-risk the asset and enable regulatory engagement.

A reported cash balance and runway into late 2027 provide a meaningful operational cushion to fund ongoing trials and data generation. This reduces immediate financing pressure, allowing the company to execute clinical plans and pursue regulatory interactions without near-term dilution risk.

bull.t: Proprietary EDO platform and regulatory designations
bull.b: A differentiated delivery platform with regulatory designations and multi-indication development provides structural competitive advantage. Platform-level data and designation status enhance the company’s ability to secure partnerships, attract scientific interest, and scale programs beyond a single asset over the medium term.

bear.b: The company remains pre-revenue and entirely dependent on clinical progress to create future commercial cash flows. Persistent operating losses mean the business cannot self-fund R&D or commercialization, making ongoing access to capital a structural risk until regulatory approvals and product sales are achieved.

bear.t: Sustained negative cash flow / high burn
bear.b: Material negative operating and free cash flow reflect continued high R&D investment and clinical spend. While burn has improved versus prior years, the scale of negative cash generation implies recurring external financing needs, which can pressure strategy, slow programs, or cause dilution if capital markets tighten.

Declining shareholders' equity signals persistent losses are eroding the capital buffer. Even with low leverage, reduced equity limits the company’s capacity to absorb development setbacks and increases dependence on external funding, raising governance and dilution risks over the medium term.
